_about: Lore data (docs/lore/README.md; decisions 257, 258): entries with facts, each fact saying who knows it. Code uses only status agreed. Facts, never lines to say.

entries.name: the town
entries.summary: The people the players fight for; what is found on the road comes home to the town.

facts.text: The town's name.
The town lies in the Blood Rot's region, at a distance from their mine.
The town and the whole region live under constant threat from Blood Rot raiders.
Everything brought home goes into the town's shared stockpile.
People rescued from captivity come to live in the town and work their trade.
Who rules or speaks for the town.

entries.name: the goblins
entries.summary: Imps, brutes and sneaks, the goblin kinds met in the land today.

facts.text: Imps, brutes and sneaks are goblins.
The goblins win by holding things, captives and ground, not by taking loot.
The imp is small and darts in and out of a fight.
The brute is big and heavy, and it stands guard.
The sneak patrols and comes at its prey from the side.
How these goblins stand to the Blood Rot: the same clan, kin in a feud, or unrelated.
Whether goblins can be bargained with, and whether one could leave its own.
Whether imps, brutes and sneaks are one people (perhaps ranks of the Blood Rot) or creatures the goblins keep.
Whether the goblins hold a castle near the town.
Who took the smith and his hammer, and why.

entries.name: the Blood Rot
entries.summary: A band of goblins born changed, who live in and around an old mine over a fallen star, worship it, and raid the region for food and people.

facts.text: The Blood Rot are a band of goblins who live in and around an old mine.
The Blood Rot's children are born changed; that is why they are called the Blood Rot.
The nearer to the mine a Blood Rot lives, the stronger and more changed it is.
What the rest of the land calls a curse, the Blood Rot thrive in.
The Blood Rot took the name as their own; to them it is a creed, not an insult.
The rot kept the Blood Rot's enemies away, and they worship its source.
The Blood Rot worship the fallen star in the deep of their mine.
The land around the mine is dead, so the Blood Rot cannot feed themselves from it, and they raid outside it for food and beasts to eat.
The Blood Rot's high priests demand bounty and sacrifice for the fallen star.
Blood Rot raiders take food, beasts and people.
Blood Rot raiders keep small camps in the region's forests.
When the Blood Rot's numbers grow too high, their raids spill into neighbouring regions.
The Blood Rot are sick and wretched.
The rot is catching: whoever touches one of the Blood Rot will rot.
The Blood Rot grow weaker the farther they go from the star, which is why their raiders are the weakest of them.

entries.name: the earlier humans
entries.summary: The humans who built the tower over the mine and died off from the rot.

facts.text: Humans who lived before built the tower over the mine.
Those humans died off from the rot, and the goblins grew stronger from it.
Who the earlier humans were: the town's forebears or a people wholly gone, and whether any survived.
Whether the earlier humans worshipped the star, and the Blood Rot took that worship from them.
